citations: Haboeck, Multivariate lookups based on logarithmic derivatives, ePrint 2022/1530, Lemma 5 (set inclusion). An honest prover holding a true inclusion and the lemma's multiplicities satisfies the fractional identity as an identity of rational functions, so the only way its instance at the sampled point fails is that the instance is undefined.

The failure set is exactly the poles: beta in the negated table entries or the negated looked-up values makes a denominator vanish, and the produced claim asserts the sums are defined as well as equal. There are at most table + lookups such points, counted as a set rather than as the degree of a polynomial, which is why this bound is one larger than the soundness bound over the same quantities.

citations: Haboeck, Multivariate lookups based on logarithmic derivatives, ePrint 2022/1530, Lemma 5 (set inclusion): over a field of characteristic p > N, two sequences of common length N satisfy the fractional-sum identity in F(X) exactly when the one is set-included in the other, with the honest multiplicities being the lookup-side count divided by the table-side count. Sequences of unequal length reduce to this by padding the shorter side with a repeated table entry, which leaves the common length at the larger of the two -- hence the machine condition on max(table, lookups) rather than on either alone.

Schwartz--Zippel root counting at the sampled bus point: clearing denominators leaves a polynomial identity in which every term omits one of the table + lookups linear factors, so its degree is at most table + lookups - 1 and a false inclusion survives a uniform point with at most that probability.

The points where a denominator vanishes are not an escape: the produced claim asserts the fractional sums are defined as well as equal, so a vanishing beta makes the claim false rather than vacuous, and no adversary gains by steering the transcript to one. The same points are the honest prover's whole failure set, which the completeness rule prices.
The inclusion is of sets, with multiples removed, and duplicate table entries are absorbed by the normalized multiplicities; no distinctness condition is checked because the lemma requires none.

zkc.rbr.sumcheck.notes: model: classical. This rule is more general than its cited mechanization in three ways, each zkc's own. It reads the degree per round, where the cited statement fixes a single global degree across all rounds. It fences applicability at 0 < d_i < |C_i|, where the source states the bound with no such hypothesis and is vacuous rather than false above one. zkc.side.consumed_anchors_are_round_mate.notes: Decided from the artifact's contract: which consumed anchor corresponds to which message role is contract knowledge, so the rule requires only that every anchor has a tie and the contract says what to. That the tie holds of this artifact is a seal judgment (zkc-E325), checked before any rule reads it.
zkc.side.consumed_anchors_are_round_mate.statement: every anchor of every claim this reduction consumes is tied by its contract to a message role of the round, so the claim it consumes and the claim it produces are about the same material

zkc.side.degrees_within_srs.notes: Discharged at: the structured reference string the suite pins. The artifact names commitments by digest and never reads what they commit to, so no decider can compare a degree against the string's length.
zkc.side.degrees_within_srs.statement: every polynomial the reduction opens has degree at most the highest power the pinned structured reference string supports

zkc.side.field_order_match.notes: discharged at: caller, when the resolved parameter is supplied
zkc.side.field_order_match.statement: the payload class the contract's challenge slots name is the field of the stated order; the artifact authenticates the class and the declared challenge space per round, and not the order

zkc.side.multiplicities_match_table.notes: Decided from the artifact: the two committed arities are read off the value profiles of the members filling the two roles.
zkc.side.multiplicities_match_table.statement: the multiplicity column holds one field element per table entry, so its committed arity equals the table's

zkc.side.prime_field_order.notes: Discharged at: the caller who states the field order. Nothing in a sealed artifact names a field  --  a payload class keys a codec and a challenge space counts a sampling set  --  so the order arrives as a stated parameter and its primality with it.
zkc.side.prime_field_order.statement: the stated field order is prime, so it is the characteristic of the field the protocol's arithmetic is over and a condition on the characteristic may be read against it

zkc.sr.from_rbr.notes: the first generic hop: consumes the same claim path's round-by-round conclusion (a path-internal premise, no external claim). The move budget t is symbolic - the derivation witness carries the budget-graded form (docs/spec/soundness.md sections 3.3-4), and t is the same variable the duplex FS hop reads (theta*(t) = t). model: classical.

citations: Damgaard, On Sigma-protocols (CPT 2010 v.2): Def. 1 (the Sigma-protocol class with special soundness), Sec. 1 (Schnorr), Sec. 5 Exercise 1 (equality of discrete logs, the Chaum-Pedersen shape), Sec. 4 Thm 2 (the OR-proof is a Sigma-protocol for R_OR, special soundness preserved)

Cramer-Damgard-Schoenmakers, Proofs of Partial Knowledge and Simplified Design of Witness Hiding Protocols (CRYPTO '94, LNCS 839) Thm 8: secret-sharing composition of special-sound three-move protocols; the OR case instantiates the 2-out-of-2 sharing (the fixtures split additively, c1 + c2 = c mod q)
Chaum-Pedersen, Wallet Databases with Observers (CRYPTO '92): the equality-of-discrete-logs instance

2-special soundness: two accepting conversations (a, e, z), (a, e', z') with e != e' on a shared commitment prefix yield the witness (Damgaard Def. 1); the covered instances are Schnorr (Sec. 1), equality of discrete logs (Sec. 5 Exercise 1), and the OR-composition (Sec. 4 Thm 2; CDS94 Thm 8), whose challenge split is a 2-out-of-2 sharing verified by a transparent check

zkc.ss.sigma.loss_display: special soundness at k = 2; information-theoretic extraction error 0 - the statistical price (k - 1)/|C| is generated by the SS => RBR edge
zkc.ss.sigma.notes: the lattice's special-soundness entry node (kernel.md 9.1.2), first registry instance: per-reduction facts enter with the arity vector (k_1..k_mu) and the sealed challenge spaces |C_i|. The entry deliberately carries no loss - the BGTZ SS => RBR edge (zkc.rbr.from_ss) generates eps_i = (k_i - 1)/|C_i|, and recording it here too would double-count on recomputation (the kzg_batch precedent). Soundness track only: special soundness does not imply round-by-round knowledge (BGTZ eprint 2023/1256 Thm 1.3), and the knowledge path (AFK's rewinding edge) is a separate uncited row. model: classical.
